questions.statement: You hear: Attention please. Friday training moves to Thursday at five in the main hall. What detail did you catch?
questions.context: Lucia listens to a school announcement about a timetable change for Friday sports.

options.text: Sports training moves to Thursday at five.
options.feedback: Correct! Moving training from Friday to Thursday at five is the stated detail, so Friday free correctly captures the announced change.

options.text: All sports training is cancelled this week.
options.feedback: The idea that training is cancelled all week fails because only Friday changes, while Thursday keeps the session at the stated time.

options.text: Sports training moves to Saturday morning.
options.feedback: The idea that training moves to Saturday fails because Saturday is never mentioned, while Thursday at five is clearly announced.

options.text: Sports training stays on Friday as usual.
options.feedback: The idea that training stays on Friday fails because the speaker explicitly moves it, so keeping Friday contradicts the announcement.

questions.explanation: Listening for specific details means catching numbers, days, and places exactly as spoken, then ignoring similar sounding distractors that change one small element.

options.text: Passengers should wait at gate twelve longer.
options.feedback: Correct! A forty minute delay to gate twelve means waiting there, so staying near the gate correctly follows the announcement.

options.text: The departure gate changed to number twenty.
options.feedback: The idea that the gate changed to twenty fails because twelve is the announced gate, and twenty twists that heard detail.

questions.explanation: Flight announcements hide key facts in polite formulas. Focus on flight number, new time, and gate to infer what passengers must do next.
